rows.bRaw: Electrical discharge machining (EDM) of nickel-based alloys such as Hastelloy involves the use of various electrode materials, with graphite increasingly favored due to its low cost, good machinability, and high sublimation temperature. Studies show that graphite electrodes with larger grain sizes yield higher material removal rates but also experience greater relative wear, while finer-grained graphite provides lower surface roughness and reduced tool wear, highlighting the influence of grain size on process efficiency and surface quality {{cite:S1#c1}}{{cite:S3#c1}}.

rows.b: Selective laser melting (SLM) produces nearly fully dense maraging steel parts with submicron grain sizes due to extremely high cooling rates, resulting in unique microstructures characterized by fine martensitic matrices and needle-shaped nanoprecipitates that contribute to age hardening. Heat treatments applied to these SLM parts not only enhance strength but also reduce residual stresses and slightly mitigate mechanical anisotropy, while also influencing corrosion resistance compared to conventionally produced maraging steels (Tan et al. 2018).

rows.b: Selective laser melting (SLM) produces maraging steel parts with near full density by selectively melting and fusing metallic powders layer by layer, enabling complex geometries and unique microstructural features such as submicron grains and fine precipitates due to rapid cooling rates up to 10^7 K/s. These microstructural characteristics contribute to enhanced strength, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance compared to conventionally produced maraging steels, although challenges remain in achieving acceptable ductility and fatigue performance (Yap et al. 2015)(Tan et al. 2018)(Haghdadi et al. 2020)

rows.b: Mobile health apps have been shown to improve health outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes by enhancing self-management behaviors, although evidence in other populations such as adolescents with type 1 diabetes remains limited and suggests a need for tailored approaches and strong adherence mechanisms (Cafazzo et al. 2012). Studies indicate that app features such as user-friendly design, real-time feedback, personalized elements, and involvement of health professionals contribute to effectiveness, yet overall app usage and sustained engagement vary significantly across settings and populations (Zhao et al. 2016)(Agarwal et al. 2018).

rows.b: Mobile health applications targeting diabetes self-management have demonstrated potential to improve health behaviors, such as increased frequency of blood glucose monitoring, particularly when incorporating features like gamification and automated data transfer (Cafazzo et al. 2012). However, evidence on their impact on glycemic control, measured by HbA1c levels, remains mixed, with some trials showing no significant difference between intervention and control groups, potentially due to varying levels of app usage influenced by contextual factors (Agarwal et al. 2018).
